studies.name: Quiet impossible architecture
studies.prompt:
Surreal mechanism: ONE calm contradiction in otherwise everyday modern architecture. The left counter plane converges toward one vanishing point and the right toward another; they meet seamlessly beneath the loaf, creating an elegant continuous surface that cannot exist. Let the angular wall behind fold into a tall empty coral recess, with a simple pale blue window on left. No classical piazzas, colonnades or old-world towers.
Drawing and medium: broad matte opaque gouache planes for the room, confident irregular DRY INK drawings for the people and objects. Figures carry searching contours and a few visible drawing corrections, while architecture has clean hard edges and a very few dry-brush breaks. The face and cloth detail stay economical and linear, not volumetrically shaded. Foreground counter forms a bold diagonal, both people occupy substantial frame height. A humane everyday event in subtly impossible space; restrained surprise, quiet visual intelligence, generous blank wall. No smooth CGI lighting or realistic painting. Make this recognizably drawn, with richer character than an anonymous mannequin.
Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: original visual identity exploration for Parallax, a philosophical video essay channel for adults. Output ONE finished 16:9 landscape illustration.
Shared encounter: a child on the LEFT in a plain blue coat holds ONE small copper-colored coin at chest height toward an adult woman shopkeeper on the RIGHT behind a counter. ONE loaf rests between them. THREE plain jars on a short shelf and ONE window establish a spare contemporary bread shop. No additional people or props. A quiet attentive encounter, no forced smiling.
Human drawing rules: warm, particular, visibly hand drawn. Rounded heads, distinct understated nose/ear/jaw contours, a few dark hair marks, a chosen cuff, garment seam and apron fold. Coherent small hands and joints, clear separation from props. Minimal facial features, at most one small eye dash and short profile mouth line. Give the child a slight forward lean and the adult an attentive incline. Detail comes from selected observed marks, not realistic skin rendering. Never bald featureless mannequins, faceted masks, cartoon mascots or photoreal bodies with erased faces.
Palette: pale chalk/ivory, dusty mineral blue, blue-black ink and restrained burnt coral/copper. Clean open areas and a few purposeful surface marks. Clearly illustrated, artsy, adult and humane. No photographic textures, glossy 3D, lens effects, text, letters, logos or watermarks. Avoid nostalgic ornate bakery decoration. Keep surreal changes in the setting or shadows, and keep the actual bodies intact.

We see the child's side in a frontal eye-level drawing; the counter bends upward around the loaf into an overhead view of the same counter; the adult's side returns to eye-level. ONE continuous counter plane folds like a broad architectural strip, with the loaf at the junction. Keep both people upright, anatomically ordinary and readable in their own spaces. The contradiction is in viewing geometry, not in broken anatomy. Window and shelf attach to broad asymmetrical wall planes, one seen frontally and one at an impossible angle.
Drawing and medium: graphic modernist drawing, spare charcoal-black and dry ink contours over large flat ivory, dusty cyan and coral painted shapes. Strong planar rhythm, angular architecture with organic human profiles. Draw a few precise marks for hands, cuffs, hair and bread. Most surfaces clean. The counter's role change should be legible from across the room, not merely a realistic L-shaped counter. No faceted faces, no tiny mosaic shards, no busy cubist still life. Adult editorial sophistication, expressive negative space and deliberate line interruptions.

studies.name: Monumental distance
studies.prompt:
Surreal mechanism: improbable architectural SCALE and DISTANCE. The actual child and shopkeeper retain their ordinary proportions and size relative to each other, but an impossibly long, extremely narrow counter stretches through a huge spare blue room between them. Compose a panoramic diagonal that carries the eye from the child at lower left to the adult at middle right; the small loaf sits at its center as the human-scale anchor. The giant window is one severely cropped pale rectangle extending beyond top edge. The three jars on a very short shelf near the adult emphasize how oversized the surrounding wall is. No giant coin, no giant food, no floating objects. Human figures should remain large enough for their gestures to read.
Drawing and medium: mature literary illustration with a few loose dry ink contours for the people and strong matte painted color masses. Pale blue architectural void occupies about half the image. Child coat deep ink blue, adult warm ivory shirt and copper apron. Long simple shadows give rhythmic depth. A few hand-drawn details convey hesitation and attentiveness; the space enlarges the feeling of separation. Unsettling but tender, no horror, no photographic architecture or cinematic rendering.

studies.name: Independent shadows
studies.prompt:
Surreal mechanism: the SHADOWS express a different relationship from the real people. The actual child holds the coin near the chest and the adult's open hand rests near the counter; their hands remain distinctly apart. On the big clean pale wall behind, their two oversized deep-blue shadows reach toward one another and their shadow fingertips meet above the shadow of the counter. The silhouettes clearly correspond to these same TWO people, but the arms have a different pose. The wall shadows are flat graphic silhouettes, no extra real people or ghostly translucent bodies. The real loaf stays untouched on the counter. This single contradiction is the central visual idea.
Drawing and medium: crisp hand-inked people and selected opaque painted fields, large calm ivory wall, minimal blue room geometry and a small copper accent on coin and cuff. Actual people at the lower half, long deliberate shadow forms in upper half; a clearly separate gap distinguishes real hands from shadows. Warm human profiles and loose specific clothing marks, no mannequin anatomy, no realistic light simulation. Bold editorial surrealism, not spooky fantasy. No miscellaneous symbols or decorative dream objects.

studies.name: Continuous changing surfaces
studies.prompt:
Surreal mechanism: a SINGLE continuous material surface quietly CHANGES ROLE across the shop. The dusty-blue counter top curls upward beyond the loaf into a broad vertical wall ribbon, then turns over and becomes the upper frame of the left window. Its thickness and color remain consistent, making the continuous counter-to-wall-to-window transformation readable. Use one graceful large curve and two purposeful folds, not tangled ribbons. The adult stands behind its normal right-hand counter section; the child stands before its normal left-hand section. The actual loaf, coin, jars and human bodies remain intact and ordinary. There is no extra separate magical object: the everyday architecture itself changes interpretation.
Drawing and medium: sophisticated surreal ink-and-gouache illustration with organic, slightly awkward hand-drawn people against broad constructed planes. Expressive contour variation, a few paint edges and small red-copper accents, lots of clean ivory. Softer and more fluid than strict constructivism while preserving a strong readable composition. Avoid 3D tubular extrusion, glossy surfaces, melted people, liquid bread and fantasy swirls. One simple continuous architectural transformation, observed human gestures and spare pictorial wit.

studies.name: Independent shadows in the constructivist style
studies.intent: Style transfer; preserve the shadow scene composition while adapting Parallax's constructivist visual language.
studies.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story, style-transfer.
Create one finished landscape 16:9 CONSTRUCTIVIST EDITORIAL illustration of the independent-shadow scene.

Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET and controls the composition, characters, gestures, object placement and central surreal idea. Input image 2 is a STYLE REFERENCE ONLY for Parallax's angular shape language, tonal weight, ink/amber/bone palette and adult editorial tone. Do not copy its extra shelves, male shopkeeper, child gesture or ordinary shadows.

Preserve from image 1: child at lower LEFT holding ONE coin near the chest, adult WOMAN shopkeeper with tied-back hair at lower RIGHT behind the counter, ONE loaf at center, left window, THREE small plain jars upper right, generous wall above the people. The adult's open palm is extended near the counter, but there is a large CLEAR GAP between the actual people's hands. Neither person touches the other. The large wall shadows of these same two people reach toward each other in a DIFFERENT pose, their fingertips MEETING at upper center. This deliberate mismatch is essential: real hands APART, shadow fingertips CONNECTED. Maintain the shadows' readable correspondence to the people, with distinct head shapes and tied-back hair. No third real person or ghost bodies.

Change the rendering to our constructivist system: bold angular silhouettes, broad color-blocked planes, strong diagonals, substantial ink shadows, flat amber window light and an open BONE wall. Strict palette ink #1C1814, amber #E5A544, bone #F0E6D0, walnut #5C4A3D and a small muted grey-green if needed. NO blue, cyan or coral. The wall shadows are dense flat ink silhouettes with precise, slightly handmade edges. Keep them conspicuous against the quiet wall.

People: angular but anatomically coherent and human through their posture. Broad smooth anonymous facial planes, distinct nose/ear/jaw outlines, no eyes or mouth, no rendered skin. Adult dark ink shirt and bone apron, child dark ink coat with a small bone cuff. Hands use a few deliberate planes with readable fingers. Clothes and architecture use broad calm shapes, a few chosen seam and fold marks. Keep selective tactile ink texture at a few edges; greatly reduce the pervasive triangulated micro-patterns and uniformly dense texture of reference 2. No polygon-mask tessellation. Hair as a few deliberate dark shapes. Serious, contemplative adult tone and clear graphic hierarchy.

Preserve the exact shadow storytelling idea without a forced smile, cartoon cuteness, anime linework, photorealism, 3D rendering, soft digital shading, extra props, text, lettering, logos, watermarks, halos or decorative symbols. The real foreground encounter is ordinary and restrained; the two joined wall shadows carry the one surreal contradiction.

studies.name: Independent shadows with additional constructivist detail
studies.intent: Selective detail refinement of the liked constructivist shadow image.
studies.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story, precise illustration refinement.
Edit the referenced Parallax constructivist shadow illustration. Add a modest but clearly visible amount of SELECTIVE DRAWN DETAIL, roughly one step richer, while preserving the image's composition, palette and visual identity.

KEEP EXACTLY: camera framing and 16:9 layout; child on left holding one small coin near the chest; adult woman with tied-back hair on right behind the counter; one loaf at center; left window and three jars upper right; angular ink/amber/bone/walnut planes; strong diagonal amber light. Actual foreground hands remain distinctly APART. The two large dark wall shadows have a DIFFERENT arm pose and their fingertips still CONNECT at upper center. Preserve those exact shadow silhouettes and their joined fingertips. Do not add another shadow, character or prop.

Add useful, visible detail in these specific places:
- Child's coat: define the lapel, collar construction, sleeve seam, a few small plain buttons and the cuff's folded edge with precise economical ink/bone marks. Two or three well-placed fabric creases follow the elbow and shoulder.
- Adult's shirt and apron: clarify collar and rolled sleeve construction, the apron edge seam, waist folds and tied bow; small irregular stitch marks only at selected edges, not an all-over pattern.
- Hands: refine finger separations, thumb pads, the wrist transition and a few knuckle creases with coherent angular drawing. Keep the same gestures and large gap between real hands.
- Hair: several purposeful grouped strand shapes following the child's hair and the adult's bun, with restrained amber edge accents. No realistic strand-by-strand rendering.
- Anonymous faces: slightly more defined ear contours, nose bridge, jaw-to-neck transition and two or three broad cheek/temple planes. Keep faces completely FEATURELESS: no eyes, brows, mouth or skin texture. Never a tessellated triangular mask.
- Shop materials: a few legible wood-grain strokes and joinery marks at the window and counter edges, simple jar lid/rim contours and a small amount of deliberate crust drawing on the existing loaf. The small coin may have a plain raised rim, with no text or emblem.

Make the added detail feel crafted and structurally observed, legible at normal viewing size. Keep broad quiet clothing planes and the open pale wall; shadows remain bold calm silhouettes. Preserve the mature editorial constructivist style and strict warm palette. Do not increase uniform grain, crosshatching or fine tessellation across every surface. No new decoration, no extra objects, no blue, no gradients, no photorealism, no 3D, no softer cartoon faces, no lettering or watermark. This is the same liked image with a little more specific drawing, not a redesign.

Replace its photographic crust rendering with an unmistakably hand-painted graphic loaf: three broad amber, ochre and walnut color planes, three simple graphic scoring slashes, subtly irregular painted edges.
